metadata.title: GloVe: Global Vectors for Word Representation (Pennington, Socher, Manning, 2014)
metadata.framework: Learning word vectors by explicit factorization of a log-bilinear co-occurrence matrix with weighted least squares
metadata.source_note: Extraction based on well-known content of Pennington et al. (2014). No arXiv version available.

nodes.name: Word co-occurrence matrix
nodes.statement: Let $X_{ij}$ denote the number of times word $j$ occurs in the context of word $i$ in the corpus. Let $X_i = \sum_k X_{ik}$ be the total count of contexts for word $i$. Let $P_{ij} = X_{ij}/X_i$ be the co-occurrence probability. The ratio $P_{ik}/P_{jk}$ for probe word $k$ encodes semantic relationships between words $i$ and $j$.

nodes.name: GloVe model
nodes.statement: The GloVe model learns word vectors $\mathbf{w}_i$ and context vectors $\tilde{\mathbf{w}}_j$ such that their dot product approximates the log co-occurrence: $\mathbf{w}_i^T \tilde{\mathbf{w}}_j + b_i + \tilde{b}_j = \log X_{ij}$, where $b_i, \tilde{b}_j$ are bias terms.

nodes.name: GloVe weighted least squares objective
nodes.statement: $J = \sum_{i,j=1}^{|V|} f(X_{ij}) (\mathbf{w}_i^T \tilde{\mathbf{w}}_j + b_i + \tilde{b}_j - \log X_{ij})^2$ where $f(x)$ is a weighting function: $f(x) = (x/x_{\max})^\alpha$ if $x < x_{\max}$, else $f(x) = 1$, with $\alpha = 3/4$ and $x_{\max} = 100$. The weighting prevents rare co-occurrences from dominating.

nodes.name: Co-occurrence ratio motivation
nodes.statement: The ratio $P_{ik}/P_{jk}$ distinguishes relevant from irrelevant probe words $k$: if $k$ is related to $i$ but not $j$, the ratio is large; if related to both or neither, the ratio is near 1. This motivates learning vectors where $\mathbf{w}_i^T \tilde{\mathbf{w}}_k - \mathbf{w}_j^T \tilde{\mathbf{w}}_k \approx \log(P_{ik}/P_{jk})$.

nodes.name: Explicit vs. implicit matrix factorization
nodes.statement: GloVe performs explicit weighted factorization of $\log X_{ij}$. Levy and Goldberg (2014) showed that Skip-gram with negative sampling (word2vec) implicitly factorizes a shifted PMI matrix: $\mathbf{w}_i^T \tilde{\mathbf{w}}_j \approx \mathrm{PMI}(i,j) - \log k$. Both methods are factorizing co-occurrence statistics; the difference is explicit vs. implicit.

nodes.name: Global vs. local training
nodes.statement: GloVe trains on the global co-occurrence matrix (aggregated statistics from the entire corpus), while word2vec trains on local context windows (one word at a time via SGD). GloVe's global approach leverages corpus-wide statistics more efficiently.

nodes.name: Competitive performance with word2vec
nodes.statement: On word analogy tasks, GloVe achieves 75% accuracy with 300-dimensional vectors trained on 6B tokens (Wikipedia + Gigaword), competitive with or slightly outperforming word2vec on most benchmarks.
